title: I’ve weirdly missed all of Taran Killam’s theatre performances!  #bro...
transcript: Ranking the SNL cast members that I've seen do live theatre. in last place through no fault of his own. I have Darrell Hammond, who I saw play a very bit cameo part in the Encores production of Call Me Madam. Nothing wrong with his performance, it was just a very small role and it was opposite Carol Kane, who outshines everyone. I’m realizing that I don't really have any bad ones on this list Next I have Alex Moffat who I saw in the Cottage and Big Gay Jamboree and I thought he was very funny in both, but maybe not a standout in either show. Next I have Cecily Strong, who I saw in The search for science for Intelligent Life in the universe. She did a really admirable job with this one person show where she played a bunch of different characters, but I actually thought some of the character work was not as clearly defined as it should have been. Next I have Jane Wickline, the newest addition to this list. Newest in all regards I just saw the show that she wrote with her writing partner Liva Pierce Dukes at Soho Playhouse and the comedy and style of it was very specifically suited to their strengths. But At the same time, I could feel some growing pains in terms of adapting their style of comedy to theatre Next I have Billy Crystal, who I saw, of course, in Mr. Saturday Night on Broadway. He got a lot of flack for his singing in this, and yes, I agree, and I think that's why he's kind of low down. But his acting was, I think, surprisingly grounded and emotionally rich. Now it's time for the trickiest entry on this list. I have Rachel Dratch, but hear me out on this! By a huge margin, she is the person on this list that I have seen do theatre the most. I saw her in Love’s Labour’s lost, Ripcord, Privacy, POTUS, high spirits, and, of course, her current role in Rocky Horror. I think those last two performances were the best work I've seen from her. It seems like we finally figured out what to do with her in theatre. Because when she does more traditional acting work in, like, standard plays, I don't think she's very good. Next I have Robert Downey Jr who, yes, did one season on SNL In the 80s. And, of course, I saw him on Broadway in McNeal a couple years ago. As much as I didn't like this play, I actually thought he did a very good job with it, and it played it perfectly to his strengths. Getting into the top four, I now have Maya Rudolph in Oh Mary. I thought it was an extremely funny performance. And she brought her particular sense of humor to the role in a way that definitely did work for me. Next I have Anna Gasteyer. And actually, the reason she's so high up is not because of her performance in Schmigadoon. It's because of the performance I saw her give in Annie at the Hollywood Bowl. She was maybe the best Miss Hannigan I've ever seen. Astonishingly good. But the top two on this list are admittedly a little bit unfair. We essentially have two theatre actors who just happened to do a season on SNL. This one being Christine Ebersole, who has many theatre credits. But I think the only time I actually saw her live was in War Paint opposite Patti LuPone. And she was excellent. But in first place, I have Michael McKean, who actually did two seasons on SNL In the 90s. And likewise, he's just a very skilled and accomplished stage actor. I've seen him in many things over the years, and it's always a pleasure.
classificationReason: Ranks SNL cast members across multiple different theatre productions (Call Me Madam, The Cottage, Big Gay Jamboree, The Search for Signs of Intelligent Life, Dukes, etc.); no single primary show.
